job.title: Unit Manager Parks Development
job.description:
About The City of Whittlesea

The City of Whittlesea is one of Australia’s fastest growing municipalities, supporting a diverse community of more than 220,000 people across established suburbs, growth areas and rural communities.
  
With continued growth comes significant investment in the parks, open spaces, sporting facilities and public realm that support connected and liveable communities.
  
This role presents an opportunity to lead the delivery of a diverse portfolio of highly visible projects that will help shape places used by the community every day.
  
About the Role
  
Reporting to the Manager Capital Delivery, the Unit Manager Parks Development is a senior leadership role responsible for the planning, design and delivery of Council’s parks, open space, sporting and public realm capital program.
  
Leading a team of experienced landscape architects and project managers, you will oversee a diverse portfolio spanning major park redevelopments, playgrounds, sports fields, streetscapes, town centres and broader open space improvements. The breadth of the program provides genuine variety, from smaller community-focused initiatives through to complex, high-profile capital works.
  
A key focus will be bringing a strong delivery and project management lens to the function. You will strengthen project governance, contract management and delivery disciplines while maintaining the design quality, creativity and landscape expertise already established within the team.
  
The role will oversee projects from design and procurement through construction and commissioning, while also directly managing selected priority projects. Acting as Superintendent across major contracts, you will work closely with contractors, consultants, government agencies, sporting clubs, community groups and internal stakeholders to deliver quality outcomes on time and within budget.
Just as importantly, this is a people leadership role. You will lead a capable and technically strong team, building on their expertise while creating greater collaboration, accountability and connection across the broader Capital Delivery department.

About You
  
You are an experienced capital delivery professional with a strong background across parks, open space, sporting, public realm or similarly complex community infrastructure.
  
Strong project and contract management capability will be important, with experience taking projects from initial planning and design through procurement, construction and completion.
  
You will understand the governance and commercial requirements of capital delivery and be comfortable managing contracts, budgets, risk and competing stakeholder priorities.
  
People leadership will be equally important. This is an intelligent, creative and technically capable team, and the role will suit someone who can provide clear direction, develop capability and encourage ideas, while bringing a strong focus on delivery and accountability.
  
A collaborative approach will be key. You will be comfortable building relationships across Council and working with government agencies, contractors, consultants and community stakeholders to navigate competing priorities and achieve practical outcomes.
  
A relevant tertiary qualification in Landscape Architecture or a similar discipline is required, together with substantial experience delivering capital infrastructure through major contracts.

job.title: Coordinator Fleet and Urban Maintenance
job.description:
About Baw Baw Shire Council

Baw Baw Shire Council is a growing municipality located on the doorstep of metropolitan Melbourne, encompassing thriving townships, rural communities and some of Gippsland’s most attractive natural landscapes.
  
With continued growth placing increasing demand on Council services and infrastructure, Baw Baw is focused on building the capability, systems and services required to support its communities into the future.
  
This creates an exciting opportunity for an experienced operational leader to join the Open Space & Maintenance team and play an important role in how Council’s fleet and urban maintenance services continue to evolve.
  
About the Role

Reporting to the Manager Open Space & Maintenance, you will provide leadership across Council’s Fleet, Workshop and Urban Maintenance functions, with responsibility for a diverse in-house workforce of approximately 20 employees.
  
You will oversee services spanning Council’s fleet and plant, workshop operations, drainage and footpath maintenance, signage, street sweeping and public amenity cleansing.
  
A key focus of the role will be people leadership. You will support and develop your supervisors, create clarity around expectations and priorities, and continue building a collaborative and accountable culture across the depot.
  
Alongside the operational leadership, you will bring a strategic lense to how these services are planned and managed. This includes strengthening governance, systems and performance reporting, managing risk and compliance, and identifying opportunities to improve service delivery as the municipality continues to grow.
  
Fleet will form an important part of the portfolio, with Council managing approximately 450 vehicles and plant across operational, pool, commuter and private-use arrangements. You will oversee long-term fleet and replacement planning, workshop capability, lifecycle management and investment decisions to ensure Council’s fleet remains safe, compliant and financially sustainable.
  
The role will also provide strategic oversight across urban maintenance, ensuring appropriate service standards, maintenance programs and systems are in place across drainage, footpaths, signage, street sweeping and cleansing.
  
About You

We are looking for an experienced operational leader who combines strong people leadership with the ability to take a broader view of service delivery, risk and continuous improvement.
  
Experience leading operational services within a complex environment will be important, with exposure to fleet, asset management or municipal maintenance highly regarded. This is less about being a technical specialist across every area and more about bringing strong leadership and a broader strategic perspective.
  
Strong people leadership will be central to success. An approachable, practical and collaborative style, combined with experience developing supervisors and operational teams, managing performance and creating clear accountability, will be highly valued.
  
A sound understanding of fleet or asset lifecycle management, operational governance, safety and risk will be important, along with the commercial awareness to manage budgets, procurement and external service providers. Experience with heavy vehicle or Chain of Responsibility requirements will be advantageous, or alternatively the ability to quickly develop this knowledge.
  
Strong communication and stakeholder skills will complement the ability to balance day-to-day operational priorities with longer-term planning and continuous improvement.
  
Relevant tertiary qualifications in asset management, business, engineering, leadership, governance, project management or a related discipline, combined with substantial relevant experience, will be required.

job.title: Taxation Compliance and Governance Lead
job.description:
Taxation Compliance and Governance Lead
Noosa Council | Noosa, QLD | $109,838 Base | $124,675 TRP
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Noosa Council to recruit an experienced Taxation Compliance and Governance Lead.
  
This is much more than a business-as-usual taxation position.
It is a senior specialist opportunity to lead Council’s response to two critical taxation compliance projects relating to Fringe Benefits Tax and Superannuation Guarantee.
  
Reporting to the Financial Services Manager, you will combine advanced technical taxation knowledge with strong project delivery capability. You will identify and quantify areas of exposure, lead remediation activities and embed governance frameworks that support sustainable compliance beyond the life of the projects.
The role will also provide specialist advice across Goods and Services Tax, contractor classification, supplier taxation obligations and other associated compliance risks.
  
Council needs someone who can do more than identify problems. You will need to translate complex legislation into practical solutions, bring clarity to accountabilities and deliver lasting improvements across finance, payroll, human resources, procurement and governance.
  
The Opportunity
This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports. Your influence will come through your technical expertise, judgement, stakeholder capability and ability to lead complex work through to completion.
You will take ownership of the end-to-end delivery of Council’s priority taxation compliance projects, ensuring milestones, deliverables and outcomes are achieved within agreed timeframes.
  
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Leading specialist compliance projects relating to Fringe Benefits Tax and Superannuation Guarantee
  • Acting as Council’s taxation and compliance specialist within Financial Services
  • Providing expert advice across FBT, GST, Superannuation Guarantee, contractor classification and supplier-related taxation obligations
  • Undertaking retrospective compliance reviews, including data analysis, risk identification and impact assessment
  • Quantifying potential exposure and developing practical remediation strategies
  • Designing and embedding fit-for-purpose governance frameworks, policies, procedures and internal controls
  • Partnering with Finance, Remuneration and Benefits, Human Resources, Procurement and Governance teams
  • Clarifying responsibilities and supporting informed decision-making across multidisciplinary teams
  • Managing engagement with external taxation advisers and specialists, ensuring quality, value for money and timely delivery
  • Preparing executive-level briefings, risk assessments, options papers and recommendations
  • Managing project scope, dependencies, milestones and progress reporting
  • Building organisational capability through structured knowledge transfer, clear documentation and practical guidance
  • Ensuring responsibility for ongoing compliance can transition effectively into operational teams at the completion of the projects
  
About You
You will be an experienced taxation, superannuation or compliance professional who is comfortable taking ownership of complex and potentially sensitive issues.
  
You will bring strong technical knowledge, but equally important will be your ability to apply that knowledge in a practical organisational environment. You will know how to move from identifying an issue to quantifying the risk, recommending a course of action and implementing a sustainable solution.
  
You’ll bring:
  • Demonstrated experience leading taxation, superannuation or compliance-focused projects within a large or complex organisation
  • Advanced knowledge of Australian taxation legislation relating to payroll and employment arrangements
  • Strong technical capability across Fringe Benefits Tax and Superannuation Guarantee
  • Knowledge of GST, contractor engagement models and supplier-related taxation obligations
  • Proven experience conducting retrospective compliance reviews and identifying regulatory risk
  • Experience supporting taxation remediation and broader governance improvement initiatives
  • Strong project governance and delivery capability, including managing scope, dependencies, milestones and reporting
  • Experience designing and implementing policies, procedures and internal control frameworks
  • Highly developed stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • The ability to translate complex legislative and technical requirements into clear, practical advice
  • Strong written capability, including the preparation of executive briefings, risk assessments and recommendations
  • The confidence to work across multidisciplinary teams while maintaining clear advisory and operational accountabilities
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach and the judgement to work through competing risks and priorities
  
You will also hold:
  • A degree in accounting, finance, business or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrated knowledge and experience in taxation, financial compliance and governance
  • A current C Class driver licence
  
Membership of, or progress towards membership of, a recognised professional accounting body would be advantageous.
  
Previous experience within local government or the broader public sector would be highly regarded but is not essential. Council will also consider candidates from complex corporate environments who can demonstrate the required taxation expertise, governance awareness and project delivery capability.
  
Why Noosa Council?
  
At Noosa Council, being “Different by Nature” reflects more than the region’s location. It represents how Council supports its people, serves its community and protects one of Australia’s most distinctive natural environments.
Based on Kabi Kabi Country, Noosa Shire is home to more than 56,000 residents and covers 872 square kilometres. Internationally recognised as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, the region offers an exceptional combination of beaches, national parks, lakes and hinterland communities.
Council employs more than 500 people and plays an important role in delivering a sustainable future for the shire.

  • LGOA Level 6 base salary of $109,838
  • Total remuneration package of $124,675, inclusive of 12% employer superannuation and 17.5% leave loading
  • Applicable salary increases under Council’s Certified Agreement 2025
  • Flexible working arrangements

  • Training, mentoring and professional development opportunities
  • The opportunity to deliver meaningful improvements that will strengthen Council’s financial governance and compliance environment
  
This is an opportunity to work where others holiday while delivering complex, high-value work that will have a lasting organisational impact.

job.description:
Civil Works Manager
North Burnett Regional Council | Mundubbera, QLD | Civil Works & Infrastructure | Circa $150K base + Accommodation + Car allowance
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with North Burnett Regional Council to recruit an experienced Civil Works Manager to provide strategic and operational leadership across Council's civil works and open spaces functions. This is an outstanding opportunity for a hands-on, visible and people-focused leader who wants to make a genuine difference.
  
This position suits a pro-active leader who will get out across the region, spend time with their teams, understand the condition of the network, visit works in progress and actively resolve the issues that impact employees and the community.
  
With teams operating across six townships, visibility matters. The successful candidate will be expected to build strong relationships with staff, provide clear direction and create an environment where people feel supported, developed and accountable.
  
The Role
  
Reporting to the General Manager Works, you will lead the delivery of Council's civil works services across a diverse regional portfolio encompassing rural and urban roads, bridges, parks and open spaces, aerodromes and cemeteries.
There is a significant opportunity to make your mark.
  
Council is rebuilding momentum across its civil works program, with a strong focus on road renewals, resheeting, resealing and bridge repairs. You'll inherit capable people within the team, while having the opportunity to strengthen leadership, develop emerging talent and improve how works are planned, prioritised and delivered.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  
  • Providing visible, hands-on leadership across geographically dispersed civil works and open spaces teams
  • Leading, coaching and developing staff while building accountability, capability and succession
  • Overseeing the delivery and maintenance of Council's rural and urban road networks and associated infrastructure
  • Developing maintenance programs and identifying renewal priorities through sound asset management practices
  • Leading the planning and delivery of Council's civil capital works program
  • Managing operational and capital budgets and ensuring resources are directed to the areas of greatest need
  • Driving improvements in productivity, plant utilisation, safety and service delivery
  • Working closely with contractors, consultants and internal teams to achieve value-for-money outcomes
  • Building trusted relationships with stakeholders and communities across the North Burnett region
  • Providing clear, consistent and evidence-based advice while following issues through to resolution.
  
The formal position description reinforces this emphasis on visible leadership, staff capability, accountability and safety alongside asset management and capital delivery.
  
About You
  
You are an experienced civil works or infrastructure professional, but importantly, you are a leader who enjoys being involved.
  
You'll be comfortable walking into a depot and talking with frontline employees, visiting a road or project to understand an issue firsthand, mentoring an engineer who wants to progress their career, and then presenting clear and credible advice to senior leadership or elected members.
  
You will bring:
  • Strong experience across civil works, roads, infrastructure maintenance or construction
  • Proven experience leading operational and geographically dispersed teams
  • A hands-on and highly visible leadership style
  • A genuine commitment to coaching, mentoring and developing people
  • Strong asset management and capital works planning capability
  • Sound commercial, financial and project management experience
  • A practical understanding of safety within civil construction and maintenance environments
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to engage equally well with frontline staff, technical professionals, executives and elected members
  • Energy, initiative and a willingness to challenge existing ways of working and implement improvements
  • High levels of integrity, accountability and follow-through.
  
Council is open-minded regarding where you have developed your experience. You may already be working within local or state government, or you may come from civil construction, consulting or another infrastructure environment and be looking to bring your experience into a broader community-focused leadership role. The client specifically confirmed that local government experience is not essential and is interested in candidates who bring energy, ideas and the ability to implement change.
  
A Civil Engineering background and RPEQ would be highly regarded although this is not essential. More important is having the technical credibility to be an informed client and provide sound leadership across the function.
  
Why Join North Burnett Regional Council?
  
This is a role where you can see the impact of your leadership.
  
You'll have the opportunity to strengthen an established team, develop future leaders, rebuild momentum across the road network and introduce new ideas that improve how Council delivers services to its communities. Council sees a genuine opportunity for innovation and more cost-effective delivery as it continues a multi-year program of rebuilding its road network.

  • Remote locality allowance

  • Relocation assistance for the successful candidate
  • Access to Council housing in Mundubbera
  
If you're a civil infrastructure professional who believes leadership means being present, developing your people, communicating clearly and taking ownership of outcomes, this is an opportunity to have a genuine impact across an entire region.

job.description:
A local council in the Northern suburbs is seeking an experienced Equity & Wellbeing Project Officer to join their team on a 3-month contract, supporting the delivery of key equity, inclusion and wellbeing initiatives.

This is a great opportunity for someone with experience across social policy, gender equality, community development or family violence prevention, looking to make an immediate impact within a busy local government environment.

The Role Working closely with the Senior Coordinator, you will provide project, operational and coordination support across the Equity, Inclusion and Wellbeing portfolio.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Supporting the planning, delivery and evaluation of community-based projects and action plans
  • Coordinating initiatives relating to gender equality and prevention of gender-based violence
  • Supporting the delivery of 16 Days of Activism activities
  • Supporting Gender/Equity Impact Assessments
  • Providing project and administrative support to the Free From Violence program
  • Coordinating events, including venues, catering, equipment and on-the-day logistics
  • Supporting community and stakeholder engagement activities
  • Facilitating and participating in external network meetings
  • Maintaining accurate budgets, financial records and project documentation
  • Managing competing priorities and ensuring projects are delivered within agreed timeframes
About You To be successful in this role, you will have:
  • Experience in project management and planning within a social policy or community-focused environment
  • Demonstrated experience in gender equality and/or prevention of gender-based or family violence
  • Experience undertaking Gender Impact Assessments or similar
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • Experience supporting community programs, projects or events
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities
  • Experience working with budgets, procurement and financial processes
  • A strong understanding of equity, inclusion and wellbeing principles
  • Local government experience is highly regarded
A relevant qualification in gender studies, public health, community development, public policy or a related field will be highly regarded.
What's on Offer
  • 3-month contract
  • Full-time hours
  • North Melbourne location
  • Opportunity to contribute to meaningful equity, inclusion and wellbeing initiatives
  • Immediate start
If you are available and have the relevant experience, apply now or contact Imogen Wade at Public Sector People for more information.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

job.title: Manager Communities & Cultural Services
job.description:
Manager Community & Cultural Services
Central Highlands Regional Council | Emerald, QLD | $210K–$252K TRP
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Central Highlands Regional Council to recruit an experienced and progressive Manager Community & Cultural Services.
  
This is much more than a traditional community services role.
  
It is an opportunity for an accomplished leader to take responsibility for a broad, highly visible portfolio of services that directly influence the lives of communities across the Central Highlands – and to help shape what those services look like into the future.
  
Council is looking for someone who enjoys solving problems, developing people and bringing structure to a diverse service portfolio. You won't be expected to arrive with every answer, but you will need the leadership capability, judgement and curiosity to find them.
  
With important foundations already being put in place, the incoming Manager will have a genuine opportunity to build momentum, strengthen governance and team capability, and put their own stamp on the future direction of the function.
  
The Opportunity
  
Reporting to the Director Communities, you will lead a diverse portfolio encompassing arts and culture, community grants, community relationships, youth, reconciliation, libraries, regional events and human and social recovery.
  
The breadth of the portfolio is what makes this opportunity different. Council isn't looking for a specialist who has spent their career focused exclusively on one element of community or cultural services. They need a leader who can see the bigger picture, bring different functions together and ensure people, resources and services are aligned with Council and community priorities.
  
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Providing strategic and operational leadership across Council's Community and Cultural Services portfolio
  • Leading, coaching and developing a diverse team, strengthening capability, accountability and performance
  • Driving the delivery and continuous improvement of community-facing programs and services
  • Leading the development and implementation of key strategies across libraries, arts, culture and heritage
  • Progressing Council's Community Grants Program and ensuring strong governance and alignment with community priorities
  • Managing budgets and resources while ensuring services demonstrate value and financial accountability
  • Building productive relationships with community organisations, government agencies, funding bodies, Traditional Owners and regional partners
  • Working closely with Councillors and SLT in providing clear, considered and evidence-based advice
  • Strengthening governance, systems and processes across the portfolio
  • Identifying opportunities to innovate and improve how Council delivers services and positive community outcomes.
About You
  
Above all, you will be a strong leader and problem solver.
  
You will be comfortable stepping into a complex environment, understanding the different moving parts and establishing what needs to happen next. You'll know how to bring people with you through change while still being prepared to make decisions, establish expectations and hold people accountable.
  
You'll bring:
  • Proven leadership experience within government, public services or another complex community-focused organisation
  • Experience leading diverse teams and developing capability in others
  • Strong governance awareness and an understanding of working within accountable service-delivery environments
  • Demonstrated ability to turn strategy into practical programs, projects and outcomes
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
  • The confidence and political awareness to work effectively with Councillors, executives and community stakeholders
  • Strong judgement and the ability to manage competing priorities and expectations
  • Experience delivering social impact and positive community outcomes
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach and willingness to challenge how things have traditionally been done
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications and/or significant experience in a comparable leadership position.
While previous local government management experience would be advantageous, Council is prepared to consider candidates from broader government, major not-for-profit and government-funded service organisations where you have led complex community-facing programs and understand the importance of governance, accountability and measurable service outcomes.
  
This could also represent an excellent next career step for a highly capable Coordinator or senior leader from a larger, complex council environment who has the breadth of experience and leadership maturity to step into management.
  
Why Central Highlands Regional Council?
  
This is an opportunity to do more than simply inherit an established service and maintain the status quo.
  
You'll join Council at a time when important work is already underway to strengthen the foundations of the function. The opportunity for the new Manager is to build on that work, develop the team and shape how these services evolve.
There are also significant priorities ahead, including a new library strategy, cultural and creative arts strategy incorporating an increased focus on heritage, and further work on Council's Community Grants Program.
  
For someone who enjoys diversity, problem solving, change and making things better, there is a genuine opportunity to make this role your own and leave a lasting impact on both the organisation and the communities it serves.
  
The opportunity offers:
  • $210,000–$252,000 Total Remuneration Package
  • Senior leadership responsibility across a broad and diverse portfolio
  • Relocation support
  • Potential access to Council accommodation
The opportunity to live and work in the Central Highlands while making a tangible contribution to its communities.
If you are an experienced community or public service leader looking for an opportunity where you can develop people, solve complex problems, improve services and genuinely influence the future direction of a regional community, we would like to hear from you.

job.title: Manager Communications & Engagement
job.description:
Manager Communications & Engagement
Central Highlands Regional Council | Emerald, QLD | Senior Leadership | Executive Package ($225-257K TRP)
  
Public Sector People are proud to partner with Central Highlands Regional Council to recruit a newly created Manager Communications & Engagement – an influential leadership role that will shape how Council communicates, engages and builds relationships with its communities.
  
Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, this position brings together the Communications and Community Engagement functions under one dedicated leader for the first time.
  
This is an opportunity to create a more connected and consistent approach across Council, strengthening community relationships while ensuring its priorities, achievements and services are communicated clearly and effectively.
  
The Role
  
You will lead an established team of approximately eight across Communications and Community Engagement, providing the direction and structure required to successfully bring the two functions together.
  
An early priority will be helping shape Council’s new Communications Strategy while improving how community consultation is planned, captured and followed through – ensuring Council effectively closes the loop with its communities.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading Council’s strategic communications and community engagement functions
  • Developing and implementing communication and engagement strategies
  • Providing strategic advice to the CEO, Mayor and senior leadership
  • Leading community consultation and strengthening stakeholder relationships
  • Supporting Council’s Community Reference Groups and ensuring feedback is effectively actioned
  • Leading corporate communications, media relations and reputation management
  • Overseeing digital and internal communications
  • Developing the team and creating clear expectations, accountability and continuous improvement.
  
This is a highly visible position with regular interaction with the CEO, Mayor and elected members, making political awareness, sound judgement and strong relationship management critical to success.
  
About You

Council is looking for a strong communications and engagement generalist rather than a specialist in one particular discipline – someone who understands how strategic communications, media, engagement, internal communications and digital work together.
  
You will bring:
  • Senior leadership experience across communications, community and stakeholder engagement
  • Strong strategic communications, media and reputation management capability
  • Experience developing and implementing communication and engagement strategies
  • Proven people leadership and the ability to bring teams together through change
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement and influencing skills
  • The confidence and judgement to work effectively with senior executives and elected members
  • Strong political awareness and experience within government or another complex stakeholder environment
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications and/or significant comparable leadership experience.
Experience within local or state government will be highly regarded, particularly given the political and community-facing nature of the position.
  
Why Join Central Highlands Regional Council?
  
This opportunity offers:
  • A newly created position with the opportunity to shape the function from the outset
  • Direct reporting access to the Chief Executive Officer
  • Leadership of an established Communications and Community Engagement team
  • Genuine influence over Council’s future communications and engagement strategy
  • Significant exposure to the Mayor, elected members, senior leadership and community
  • The opportunity to improve how Council engages with its communities and tells its story.
This is an opportunity to do more than manage an existing communications function. You will have the mandate to bring two areas together, establish the strategy and reshape how Council communicates and engages with the Central Highlands community.
  
Be part of something that matters, with like-minded people who truly care.
